title: Targeting notch signaling pathway in breast cancer stem cells through drug repurposing approach.
authors: Pathak, Yamini; Camps, Ihosvany; Mishra, Amaresh; Tripathi, Vishwas
one_liner_zh: 该文通过药物重定位筛选FDA药物靶向Notch通路中的γ-分泌酶复合物，虽涉及分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Breast cancer is recognized globally as one of the leading causes of malignant morbidity. It is a heterogeneous disease that accounts for 30 percent of all women diagnosed with cancer. To bring an anti-cancer drug from the bench to the bedside is an expensive and time-consuming process. The drug repurposing approach targets new enemies (new diseases) with old weapons (known drugs). The present study identified an FDA-approved drug targeting the gamma-secretase complex involved in the Notch signaling pathway in breast cancer stem cells (BCSCs). A literature survey and in-silico study identified Venetoclax as a gamma-secretase inhibitor (GSI) from 1615 FDA-approved drug compounds. In-silico docking potential of Venetoclax was better than the standard gamma-secretase inhibitor RO4929097. Also, the molecular dynamics simulations of 200 ns confirmed the stability of the Venetoclax-gamma-secretase complex. These findings suggest that the use of Venetoclax represents a potential gamma-secretase inhibitor in breast cancer stem cells. Eventually, the in vitro and clinical evaluation will be needed to confirm the potential chemopreventive and treatment effects of Venetoclax against breast cancer and breast cancer stem cells. Venetoclax appeared as the most promising drug of the 1615 FDA-approved drugs. Our in-silico findings suggest that Venetoclax may act as a gamma-secretase inhibitor against the Notch signaling pathway in breast cancer stem cells.
abstract_zh: 乳腺癌在全球范围内被公认为恶性肿瘤发病的主要原因之一。它是一种异质性疾病，占所有确诊女性癌症患者的30%。将抗癌药物从实验室带到临床是一个昂贵且耗时的过程。药物再利用策略旨在用旧武器（已知药物）对抗新敌人（新疾病）。本研究识别了一种FDA批准的药物，靶向乳腺癌干细胞（BCSCs）中Notch信号通路中的γ-分泌酶复合物。通过文献调研和计算机模拟研究，从1615种FDA批准的药物化合物中鉴定出Venetoclax作为γ-分泌酶抑制剂（GSI）。Venetoclax的计算机模拟对接潜力优于标准γ-分泌酶抑制剂RO4929097。此外，200纳秒的分子动力学模拟确认了Venetoclax-γ-分泌酶复合物的稳定性。这些发现表明，使用Venetoclax代表了乳腺癌干细胞中一种潜在的γ-分泌酶抑制剂。最终，需要体外和临床评估来确认Venetoclax对乳腺癌及乳腺癌干细胞的潜在化学预防和治疗效果。Venetoclax在1615种FDA批准的药物中脱颖而出，成为最有前景的药物。我们的计算机模拟发现提示，Venetoclax可能作为γ-分泌酶抑制剂，针对乳腺癌干细胞中的Notch信号通路发挥作用。
